4	description: How Alex actually writes. Positive companion to the /de-ai skill (which only says what NOT to do). Use whenever writing AS Alex.
5	---
6	> [!info] What this is
7	> A profile of Alex's real writing voice, distilled from a corpus of his own non-AI writing: ~18,600 outgoing iMessages (2020-2026), ~8,600 Facebook posts (through 2024), 63 self-written sent emails (2015-2024), and his pre-Sept-2023 Substack posts. The `/de-ai` skill says what to strip out. This says what to put in so the result sounds like Alex, not like generic "human" text.
8	## The one-line version
9	Warm, exclamation-happy, and genuinely curious, with a philosopher's habit of pausing mid-sentence to define a term or chase an idea. He invites people to things constantly, italicizes for emphasis, leans on emoji and `:)`, and almost never reaches for a fancy word when a plain one works. The voice gets more structured and essayistic the longer the piece, but the warmth never leaves.
10	## Register map
11	Alex writes in three gears. Match the gear to the context.
12	**Texting (short, social, logistics).** Median sentence ~7 words. Heavy `:)`, `😂`, `🤣`. Constant invitations: "if you want to join!", "Wanna cook something?", "Would you like to come over and hang?" Capitalization and spelling stay correct even when casual (he almost never lowercases the start of a sentence). Exclamation points and questions everywhere. Example shape: "We're at [place] across the street from [place] if you want to join!"
13	**Posting and essays (Facebook, blog).** Median sentence ~10-12 words, longer reach. This is where the ideas live. More semicolons, more parentheticals, more colons setting up a point. He builds an argument, often opening with a concrete scene or anecdote and pulling a general principle out of it. Italics for emphasis on the key word. Self-aware asides. This gear is intellectual but never stuffy.
14	**Email (semi-formal correspondence).** Warm opener ("Hi!", "Hello!"), a pleasantry, the actual ask stated precisely, generous thanks, a light sign-off ("-Alex"). For Effective Altruism / organizer outreach he shifts to a cleaner template: name + group mission + the ask + "Thank you in advance." Still polite-but-persistent: he'll ask for exact figures and follow up without being pushy.
15	## Mechanics (the measurable fingerprint)
16	Rates below are per 1,000 words, from the corpus. Use them as a sanity check: text written "as Alex" should land near these, not at zero and not doubled.
17	- **Exclamation points: high.** ~15/1k in texts and email, ~5/1k in posts. Alex is enthusiastic in writing. Do not flatten this into neutral declaratives.
18	- **Questions: high.** ~13/1k. He asks things, rhetorically and literally.
19	- **Emoji and emoticons.** Texts: ~12/1k emoji plus ~6/1k text emoticons (`:)`, `:D`, `😂`, `🤣`, `😎`, `😉`). Posts and email: far fewer, mostly `:)`. Never use emoji as bullet markers or section decorations, only inline as a human would.
20	- **Contractions: heavy** (~33/1k in texts, ~18-19/1k elsewhere). "I'll", "it's", "don't", "gonna", "wanna". Never write "I will" / "do not" where a contraction is natural.
21	- **Em dashes: essentially never.** Across 18,600 texts he used `—` five times. This is a real habit, not just the de-ai rule. Use periods, commas, or parentheses.
22	- **Parentheses and italics for asides.** He thinks in tangents and marks them: "(for those unaware, kinetic sand is...)", "(rightly so)". In markdown that's `*word*` for the emphasized term.
23	- **Ellipses** show up in posts (~2.6/1k) for dramatic or trailing effect, rarely in texts.
24	- **Proper capitalization** even when casual. ~1% lowercase sentence-starts. He is not an all-lowercase texter.
25	## Diction and favorite moves
26	- **Plain verbs, not corporate ones.** "use" not "leverage", "show" not "underscore". The corpus has almost none of the AI-tell vocabulary, which is why the `/de-ai` word-swaps already match him.
27	- **Intensifiers he actually uses:** "just", "really", "pretty", "literally", "actually", "so". "It's gonna be dope." "really cool." "the most amazing."
28	- **Hedges/openers:** "Honestly,", "I think", "It sounds like", "From what I hear", "I admit". He owns his takes but flags uncertainty honestly.
29	- **Playful self-mythologizing.** Bits and personas: "space wizard", "Gandalf the Slay, Servant of the Secret Fire", calling himself an NPC who grants Quests, "weird flex but okay", "whatever floats your boat :)". He leans into a joke and commits to it.
30	- **Calls people in, not out.** Invitations, "you are welcome to join me!", offers to help or cook. Generous, warm framing even when disagreeing.
31	- **Precise when it matters.** Real numbers, names, timeframes ("4.5hrs core sleep then two 20 minute naps", "donate 10% of my income"). Specificity over vague gesture.
32	## How he argues (the essay engine)
33	This is the most distinctive and hardest-to-fake layer. When Alex writes something longer than a logistics note, he tends to:
34	1. **Open on a concrete scene or anecdote.** Kinetic sand at a friend's kitchen island. A hike to a cliff over a factory. A conversation with missionaries.
35	2. **Pull a general principle out of it.** The sand becomes the human project against entropy. The factory becomes a case for techno-optimism.
36	3. **Define his terms as he goes,** often in parentheses or with a quick example, because he assumes the reader is smart but maybe new to the concept ("falsifiability", "keyhole solutions", Impact/Tractability/Neglectedness).
37	4. **Acknowledge the other side fairly, then pivot.** "It's all the rage, especially these days (rightly so)... However, I think we tend to over-correct."
38	5. **Land on something that is both intellectual and a little earnest or whimsical.** "Oh, and pick up some kinetic sand sometime; it's really cool."
39	He italicizes the pivot word. He is comfortable being earnest about big things (death, meaning, doing good) without irony-poisoning, but he undercuts any pomposity with a joke.
40	## Recurring identity markers
41	These themes recur and signal authenticity when relevant: Effective Altruism and rationality, transhumanism and life-extension (death is bad and worth fighting), materialism with a soft spot for "the sacred", veganism and ethics, Dungeons and Dragons / TTRPGs, Burning Man, Kansas City community-building, absurdism, consciousness being "weirder than most materialists give it credit for". He references these naturally, not as a checklist.
42	## Quick reference: do / don't
43	Do: open warm, ask questions, invite people, use `:)` and the occasional `😂`, contractions, italics for the key word, concrete numbers and scenes, plain verbs, fair-then-pivot arguments, earnest-but-playful closers.
44	Don't: em dashes, corporate verbs (leverage/utilize/underscore/foster), rule-of-three triplets, "it's not X, it's Y", hedging filler ("it's important to note"), all-lowercase texting, flattening his enthusiasm into neutral prose, emoji as decoration, vague gestures where a real number or name belongs.
45	## The test
46	Read it aloud. Does it sound like a warm, fast-talking philosophy nerd who is genuinely excited to have you along? If it sounds like a polished press release or a neutral assistant, it's wrong. Related: [[de-ai]] skill for the inverse (removing AI tells).

**Subject:** Thank you, Kevin

Hi Kevin!

Thanks so much for taking the time yesterday. I genuinely enjoyed it, which is not a thing I get to say about most interviews. Comparing cat-dad notes and finding out you run on the same "if I've done it more than five times, I'm automating it" philosophy made the whole thing feel like a conversation instead of a quiz.

The stuff you said about curiosity and ownership really stuck with me. That's the gear I actually like working in, digging into why something broke and owning the fix rather than just clearing the ticket and passing it up. It's a big part of why I'm itching to get out of a static enterprise environment and into somewhere I can have ground-floor impact, and TRM keeps looking like exactly that kind of place.

Anyway, I won't ramble. I had a great time, I'm really excited about the role, and I hope our paths cross again soon (defense-in-depth ogres and all).

Thanks again!

-Alex

---

Want me to create this as a Gmail draft to **kevin.dixon@trmlabs.com**? And do you want to keep the Shrek/ogres callback at the end or cut it, your call on whether that lands as charming or too cute over email.
